modifications: Entries were selected, normalised (HTML removed, years parsed, headline titles shortened to about 100 characters with an ellipsis), merged and de-duplicated across sources, ranked, capped per day and category, and sorted. Summaries keep the source wording. did_you_know facts are either Wikipedia "Did you know" hooks (text only, reformatted) or one-sentence rewordings of existing entries (prefixed with the date, possibly shortened). Image links are unmodified Wikimedia URLs.

did_you_know.fact: On October 4, 1983: Richard Noble sets a new land speed record of 633.468 miles per hour (1,019.468 km/h) at the Black Rock Desert in Nevada.
On October 4, 1965: Pope Paul VI begins the first papal visit to the Americas.
On October 4, 1957: Sputnik 1 becomes the first artificial satellite to orbit the Earth.
On October 4, 1895: Horace Rawlins wins the first U.S. Open Men's Golf Championship.
On October 4, 1795: Napoleon first rises to prominence by suppressing counter-revolutionary rioters threatening the National Convention.
